summary: Standard independent functional review of all 20 changed paths. The encoded-byte poison-copy correction is sound, but the default Azure REST requests omit the required request date header.

changed_files.lines_changed: 1-215 reviewed, with worker and dispatch context

findings.title: Supply a request date for Azure Queue REST authorization
findings.problem: Every operation supplies Authorization and x-ms-version but neither Date nor x-ms-date. Azure Storage REST requires a request date (see Microsoft Learn Queue Get Messages / Put Message request headers and Authorize with Microsoft Entra ID). urllib does not add it. With the shipped default transport and a valid injected bearer token, requests are therefore rejected rather than leasing, deleting, releasing or moving messages. The worker catches receive failures and backs off indefinitely. This is an adapter wire-contract defect, not missing managed-identity wiring. Recorder tests accept arbitrary headers, so their passing results do not establish this contract. No live-service reproduction was performed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fresh RFC 1123 UTC x-ms-date in _call, for example using email.utils.formatdate(usegmt=True), before invoking the transport. Add an offline contract-enforcing transport test that refuses calls without a parseable current x-ms-date, covering receive, poison POST, ack and release. References: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/get-messages and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/authorize-with-azure-active-directory (not retrieved during this review).

positive_changes: Poison copies cap UTF-8 bytes at 45,000: base64 is at most 60,000 bytes, with the XML wrapper still below 65,536. Truncated multibyte prefixes remain valid UTF-8 and explicitly report original byte length.
Poison storage must return 201 before deletion; failed writes retain the leased original.
Delivery six is poisoned before task execution; malformed task parsing is routed to poison. Missing identity and malformed XML produce retryable errors rather than acknowledgement.
Message IDs are path-quoted and pop receipts query-encoded; release uses zero visibility without rewriting message text.
Worker context confirms post-before-ack, retry/backoff on receive faults, and unchanged fail-closed command-line serve.
testing_recommendations: Add request-header contract tests as described in finding 1.
Add offline count-five/count-six boundary, missing identity, release 404/error, poison-success/delete-failure, and fresh-token-per-call tests.
The supplied queue, worker, dispatch and dependency tests were read, not executed by this reviewer.
recommended_actions: Fix finding 1 and obtain an independent exact-new-head review before coordinator publication.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: Managed identity, postback fencing, serve wiring, deployed identity, hosting and restart/restore proofs remain later-slice concerns. No epic acceptance inferred.
Publication/force-push wording is internally inconsistent; not a queue source defect. Supplied identities and clean status are coordinator-verified, not independently executed Git checks.

The supplied transcript records commands and author summaries, but folds many stdout blocks and pipes output through tail/grep. Test counts and clean-tool claims are attributed to coordinator/native evidence, not independently verified exit statuses or tool versions.

risk_assessment: High: Azure REST request-contract defect in the bounded queue adapter. No broad production or security assessment performed.
